sprint_reviewed: Live PR Approval Gate and Safe Branch Probe Sprint
reviewer_sprint: Live PR Approval Gate Implementation Review and Agent-Operated PR Readiness Sprint
summary: All approval gate guards are correctly implemented. 11 tests pass. The publish-permission-probe command is read-only. Critical weakness: publisher.py still has a stub that returns status='published' with no actual branch creation, commit, or PR operation. PR body lacks specific evidence file paths. Words PR_SUMMARY.md references outdated target. publish-pr command not yet implemented.

claims.claim: GITHUB_TOKEN is never read by check_approval() — only PLUGIN_EXAMPLES_LIVE_PUBLISH_APPROVAL env var is read
publish_examples() accepts approval_token, repo_access_ready, pr_permission_ready parameters

claims.risk: LOW — only enforced at CLI level, not inside publish_examples(). If publish_examples() is called directly with dry_run=False, no conflict guard fires. Current code path always goes through CLI.
claims.note: Acceptable: publisher uses dry_run flag directly. CLI is the entry point. Direct calls in tests use dry_run= explicitly.

claims.risk: NONE — branch_name is always set to pipeline/{run_id}/{family} at line 117, which can never be 'main' for any real run_id.

claims.claim: probe-publish-permissions command exists and is always read-only (GET requests only, no branch/commit/PR created)
publish-permission-probe.json output contains probe_is_read_only=True and live_publish_authorized=False always
11 tests in TestLivePRApprovalGate cover all blocked reasons and probe behavior
Approval token value never stored in evidence files or logs
claims.code_reference: approval_gate.py: check_approval() only reads token and compares — never writes. publisher.py: blocked_reason constants never echo token value.

claims.claim: Publisher implements actual branch creation, commit, and PR creation after all guards pass
claims.code_reference: publisher.py:184-185 — result.status = 'published' with no actual GitHub operations
claims.test_reference: No test for actual PR creation (stub not tested for real output)
claims.risk: HIGH — If called with dry_run=False, GITHUB_TOKEN, valid approval token, and all checks passing, the code returns status='published' but creates NO branch, NO commit, NO PR. The stub is misleading: it implies success but does nothing.
claims.fix_plan: Add publish-pr command with dry-run simulation mode. Real live PR implementation is gated behind followup-agent-operated-live-pr-creation taskcard.

additional_weaknesses.weakness: PR target listed as 'aspose/aspose-plugins-examples-dotnet' — the old central placeholder. Correct target is 'aspose-words-net/Aspose.Words.LowCode-for-.NET-Examples'.
additional_weaknesses.risk: MEDIUM — Misleading documentation could cause PR to be sent to wrong repo
additional_weaknesses.fix_plan: Update PR_SUMMARY.md line 5 to correct family-specific target

additional_weaknesses.weakness: PR body evidence section lists generic text ('Source-of-truth proof verified', etc.) without specific file paths. Reviewers cannot trace evidence back to actual files.
additional_weaknesses.risk: LOW — Cosmetic, does not affect safety. PR is informational only.
additional_weaknesses.fix_plan: Add specific evidence file path references to PR body (e.g., workspace/verification/latest/{family}-source-of-truth-proof.json)

additional_weaknesses.weakness: No publish-pr subcommand exists. There is no command to simulate the full PR creation flow before going live.
additional_weaknesses.risk: MEDIUM — Without a simulation command, there is no dry-run rehearsal of the exact PR that would be created

fixes_applied_this_sprint: pr_builder.py updated: evidence section includes specific file path references
publish-pr command added to __main__.py with dry-run simulation mode

remaining_stub.note: Real live PR implementation (branch creation, git commit, gh pr create) is intentionally deferred. It will be implemented in followup-agent-operated-live-pr-creation sprint when human gives explicit approval.
